FILES TO CREATE — exactly these four, plus one edit to a fifth file:
1. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts` (the recipe)
2. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx` (the component)

Do NOT touch: `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx`, `ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/` (any file), `overrides/app/components/swatch-group/` (doesn't exist, don't create it), `translations/*.json`, `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` (Tier 1, absolute — if you think you need a new token, STOP and report back instead of adding one).

## Why the sequencing matters (same as Step 2)

`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts` walks for `*.css.ts` files declaring `parts:` and asserts a sibling `index.tsx` exists. Author recipe → registration → component, and make sure both files exist before your final verification pass.

## Design values — pulled directly from Figma just now for this exact component (node 40000307:13867, "ColourOptions", within Zimmermann_Design_System_2026), not estimated

This is a **vertical stack**: a label row, then a swatches row, `gap: 8px` between them.

- **Root container**: `display: flex; flexDirection: column; gap: var(--zimm-scale-xs)` (xs = 8px, confirmed in `overrides/app/theme/foundation/spacing.ts:11`). No background on the root — background lives per-swatch (already handled by the atom).
- **Label row** (`labelContainer`): horizontal flex, `height: 24px`, `gap: var(--zimm-scale-xs)` (8px) between the label-group and the pagination controls. The label-group takes available space (`flex: 1 0 0`) so pagination sits pinned to the right — this is what "right-aligned pagination" means structurally, not an absolute-position hack.
  - **Label-group** (the "Colour: Bay Blue" text): horizontal flex, `gap: 4px` (use `var(--zimm-scale-2xs)`, confirmed 4px in `spacing.ts:10`) between two inline text pieces: a static "Colour:" and the dynamic colour name.
  - **Text styling for both pieces**: `textStyle="caption"` — verified as an EXACT match against the Figma spec (12px size, 18px line-height, 500 weight, 0 letter-spacing) by reading `overrides/app/theme/foundation/typography.ts` directly: `caption` resolves to `fontSizes['3xs']` (12px), `lineHeights['2xs']` (18px), `fontWeights.medium` (500), `letterSpacings.sm` (0) — all four dimensions match the Figma style ("Default/Caption-strong") precisely. Use the `textStyle` prop, per this codebase's styling hierarchy (never a raw fontSize) — this is set in the recipe, not as a bare Chakra key, and `textStyle` itself stays a bare string (there's no `var()` substitute for the composite expansion, see `.claude/rules/css.md`).
  - **Text colour**: `var(--zimm-color-text-default)` (confirmed exists, `zimmTokens.ts:46`, resolves to grey[900]/#191919, matching Figma's `text/default` reference exactly).
  - **Truncation is an explicit design requirement, not optional**: Figma's own interaction annotation on this exact node reads *"If Label/Colour name is longer, use truncation."* The dynamic colour-name piece must truncate with ellipsis when it overflows — the static "Colour:" label must never truncate (give it `flexShrink: 0` or equivalent so only the name piece shrinks/truncates: `flex: 1 0 0`, `minWidth: 0`, `overflow: hidden`, `textOverflow: 'ellipsis'`, `whiteSpace: 'nowrap'`).
- **Pagination controls**: two 24×24px button boxes (left chevron, right chevron), each containing a 16×16px icon, sitting after the label-group in the label row. Figma's own interaction annotation on this exact node states verbatim: *"Pagination appears if there are more than 4 swatches. If chevron is clicked, the next set of swatches appears."* This directly confirms the mechanism — only render these controls when there are more than 4 populated colours, and clicking advances/retreats a fixed 4-wide window over the populated values array.
- **Swatches row**: horizontal flex, `width: 100%`, items sit **directly adjacent with ZERO gap between them** — confirmed directly from the Figma export: the 4-swatch example measures exactly 192px total width for four 48px-wide swatches (4 × 48 = 192, no gap contribution). Do not add a gap here — that would be a real deviation from the design, not a stylistic default.

## The recipe — `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts`

Export name: `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` (exact casing — must not collide with any base SFCC recipe name; base registers `SwatchGroup`, and this name is safely distinct, but double-check `overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s `INTENTIONAL_MERGES` list still only contains `['Button','Header','ListMenu']` if you want to confirm no allow-list dependency exists).

`parts: ['root', 'label', 'labelName', 'swatches', 'pagination', 'pageButton']` — six parts:
- `root` — the outer vertical flex container
- `label` — the label row (horizontal flex containing labelGroup + pagination)
- `labelName` — the dynamic colour-name text piece specifically (the one that truncates) — the static "Colour:" text can use inline styling within `label` or its own minimal styling, your call, but the truncation behaviour must land specifically on the dynamic name piece
- `swatches` — the horizontal row of `<ZimmColourSwatch>` children
- `pagination` — the wrapper around the two chevron buttons
- `pageButton` — each individual 24×24 chevron button

Make sure every part your `index.tsx` reads via `styles.*` is declared here — `recipeParts.test.ts` checks this mechanically and will fail the build if you read a style key that isn't declared. Read the sibling `zimmColourSwatch.css.ts` (Step 2's recipe) for the established comment style and structure to match.

Every colour/space value must be `var(--zimm-*)` — no bare Chakra key, no raw px/rem/em/hex. Self-check with `grep -nE "#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}|[0-9]+px|[0-9.]+rem|[0-9.]+em" overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts` before you're done — code-level hits (not comments) should be zero. **Any Figma value you can't map to an existing token: STOP and report back rather than inventing one or adding to `theme/foundation/`.**

**If you need a responsive breakpoint step for anything** (unlikely for this component, but if you do), it must be an explicit media query off `BP` in `overrides/app/theme/components/footerShared.ts` — never Chakra's array shorthand (`['2xs','2xs','xs','xs']`), which fails this codebase's bare-token guard at every array element.

## The component — `index.tsx`

Props type (declare at top, JSDoc each field):
```ts
type ZimmColourSwatchValue = {
  value: string;
  name: string;
  href?: string;
  imageUrl?: string; // undefined = index image not populated (AC 5)
};
type ZimmColourSwatchGroupProps = {
  label: string;              // SFCC attribute display name, e.g. "Colour"
  selectedName?: string;
  selectedValue?: string;
  values: readonly ZimmColourSwatchValue[];
};
```

Import and compose `ZimmColourSwatch` from `../../atoms/zimmColourSwatch` (relative path within `ui-kits/`, consistent with how sibling molecules import sibling atoms — check `zimmProductMeta/index.tsx` or similar for the exact import convention used in this codebase).

**This is a pure presentational leaf — no data-fetching hook of any kind.** `useIntl()` is the one exception, explicitly allowed per this codebase's `components.md` rule (a leaf may call `useIntl`/`useUiCopy` since both read from a Provider mounted above the route tree, not a per-page fetch). Use `const intl = useIntl();` — never destructure it (`@typescript-eslint/unbound-method`).

**Three ACs live here as branch logic — this is the core of the component:**

1. **Filter first** — `const populated = values.filter((v) => Boolean(v.imageUrl));`. This implements AC 5 (a colour variation whose index image is not populated is not rendered and not surfaced to the shopper) and it belongs HERE, not at the page level, because this component's own test file is where its contract must be provable — the PDP page has no test file of its own. This is a **content-population** check, structurally different from stock/orderability — do not filter on any stock-related field, only on whether `imageUrl` is present.
2. **`populated.length <= 1`** → render the label row ONLY (the "Colour: Bay Blue" text), no `swatches` node at all, no `radiogroup` role anywhere. This is AC 1. Filter-then-count matters: an unpopulated variation must never count toward "there are multiple colours" — so count `populated.length`, never `values.length`.
3. **`populated.length > 1`** → render the label row AND the swatches row. For each populated value, render `<ZimmColourSwatch name={value.name} imageUrl={value.imageUrl!} href={value.href} isSelected={...} isFocusable={...} />` (the `!` is safe here — you just filtered on `Boolean(v.imageUrl)`, TypeScript may still need a non-null assertion or you can restructure the filter to narrow the type; either is fine, but if you use `!`, it needs a one-line comment explaining why it's safe here specifically, per this codebase's non-null-assertion rule). `isSelected = value.value === selectedValue`. `isFocusable = isSelected || (!selectedValue && index === 0)` — this is base SFCC's own exact roving-tabindex rule (see `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/swatch-group/index.jsx` or the extracted `renderDefaultVariationAttribute` in our own `product-view/index.tsx` for the same logic already in this codebase).
4. **Pagination**: only when `populated.length > 4`. Maintain a windowing state (e.g. `useState` for the current page start index) and render only a 4-wide slice of `populated` at a time, plus the two chevron buttons. **Paging moves the window, not the selection** — if the selected colour is off-window, it stays selected (state doesn't change), it's just not visible until paged back into view. Each chevron is a real `<button>` (not a styled span pretending to be one) with a clear `aria-label` (e.g. "Previous colours" / "Next colours" — use `intl.formatMessage`, not a literal string), and is disabled at its end of the range (left chevron disabled when the window is already at the start, right chevron disabled when it's already at the end).
5. Use `ChevronLeftIcon` / `ChevronRightIcon` (already exist in `overrides/app/components/icons/zimm.tsx`, confirmed) rendered via `ZimmIcon` from `overrides/app/components/icons` (check that module's actual export/usage pattern by reading it first — don't guess the API).

**Label text**: reuse base SFCC's own message id, don't invent a new one — `swatch_group.selected.label`, `defaultMessage: '{label}:'` (check `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/swatch-group/index.jsx` for the exact id/defaultMessage string, use it verbatim so this stays consistent with base's own i18n key rather than fragmenting translation keys). Render the static "Colour:" piece from this, then the dynamic name piece (`selectedName` when available) separately per the two-text-node structure Figma shows, with the ellipsis-truncation behaviour on the name piece only.

**Keyboard**: `role="radiogroup"` on the swatches wrapper with an `aria-label` (use the `label` prop). `onKeyDown` moving focus across the rendered `<ZimmColourSwatch>` children with Arrow keys — mirror the roving-focus pattern in base `swatch-group/index.jsx` (read it) or the equivalent logic already extracted in our own `product-view/index.tsx`'s `renderDefaultVariationAttribute`. Arrows move **focus only**, not selection/navigation — this matches today's live behaviour, since `product-detail` (Step 4, not yet built) will pass no `onVariationChange`-equivalent, so there's nothing to trigger on arrow press beyond moving which element has focus. Activation is the anchor's native Enter key (inherited for free from the atom's `<ColourSwatchLink>`). Space does not activate an anchor element (a native browser/HTML behaviour, not a bug) — add a one-line comment noting this is an inherited parity gap versus a true native radio input, not a new regression introduced here.

## The story — `index.stories.tsx`

`title: 'Commerce/ZimmColourSwatchGroup'`. Local `MemoryRouter` decorator (same reason as the atom's story — no router in `.storybook/preview.tsx`).

Named exports:
- `Default` — 4 populated colours, one selected.
- `SingleColour` — exercises AC 1 (one populated value, label only, no swatches).
- `WithUnpopulatedVariations` — 5 values total, 2 without `imageUrl` (exercises AC 5's filter — should render only 3 swatches).
- `NoneSelected` — no `selectedValue` passed.
- `Paginated` — 6 populated colours, exercising the chevron controls.

Add a `play` function on `Default` asserting arrow-key focus movement across the swatches (use `@storybook/test`'s `userEvent`, per this codebase's testing conventions — query via `within(canvasElement)`, never `document` directly). Add a second `play` on `Paginated` asserting that clicking the "next" chevron advances the visible window AND that the previously-selected swatch's selection state survives paging (even if it scrolls out of the visible window and back).

## The test — `index.test.tsx`

Wrap renders in `MemoryRouter` + `IntlProvider` (the latter because `useIntl` throws outside one — confirmed pattern, check how `zimmProductStyleCode/index.test.tsx` or similar wraps this). **Mock `ZimmIcon`** at the smallest surface — `vi.mock('app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon', () => ({ ZimmIcon: () => null }))` or similar (check the actual export name/path by reading the real module first) — this is a known, documented Vitest gap (`ZimmIcon` throws under Vitest due to a base-icons-barrel side effect), not something you need to investigate further, just work around it per this codebase's established pattern.

Seven required assertions:
1. One populated colour → `queryAllByRole('radio')` has length 0, and the rendered text reads "Colour: Bay Blue" (or whatever your test's fixture name is — match the AC's own example).
2. Three populated colours → 3 elements with `role="radio"`.
3. Exactly one has `aria-checked="true"`, and it corresponds to `selectedName`.
4. **AC 5**: 5 values, 2 without `imageUrl` → exactly 3 radios render, and neither of the two excluded colours' `name` appears anywhere in `container.textContent`.
5. **AC 5 vs orderability**: construct a value that has `imageUrl` set (regardless of any stock-like field you might be tempted to add) and confirm it renders — proving the filter keys on image population, not on stock/orderability (this component's prop type doesn't even carry a stock field, so this assertion is really about confirming you didn't accidentally add one).
6. Reducing 3 colours to 1 populated (i.e. 2 of the 3 have no `imageUrl`) triggers the AC 1 label-only branch (no radios).
7. Exactly one rendered element has `tabIndex === 0` (or `tabindex="0"` as a DOM attribute) at any given time.

**Mutation check — do this for real, report before/after output, don't just assert it would work.** Temporarily delete or neuter your `values.filter((v) => Boolean(v.imageUrl))` line (e.g. make it a no-op that returns `values` unfiltered), re-run the AC-5 test, confirm it actually FAILS (should now show 5 radios instead of 3, or show an excluded colour's name in the text), then restore the real filter and confirm the test passes again. Report both outputs.

## Verification — run yourself, report exact output

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run lint
npm run test
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs
```

Baselines on this branch right now (after Steps 1+2): tsc 0 errors; test 27 files/417 tests (you're adding one new test file, so expect 28 files and MORE than 417 tests — report exact numbers); lint 20 problems/4 errors (pre-existing, not yours)/16 warnings, exit 1; audit:tokens exactly 4 unacknowledged/22 acknowledged, exit 1 — your new files must add zero new unacknowledged findings.

Also run and report:
```
grep -c "ZimmColourSwatchGroup" overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts
```
Must return exactly 2.

```
npm run test 2>&1 | grep -i "zimmColourSwatchGroup\|recipeParts"
```
Confirm `recipeParts.test.ts` collected and passed a case for this new recipe by name.

```
grep -n "toLowerCase\|useProduct\|useCurrentBasket\|commerce-sdk-react" overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx
```
Should return nothing (no data hooks, and no reason to reference `toLowerCase` in this molecule).

Report back: full output of every command, confirmation of exactly which files were created/edited, and the mutation check's before/after output for the AC-5 filter test.

5	 * variation's product photo. Two parts: `swatch` is the outer clickable box (geometry,
6	 * background, border, focus ring); `image` is the element carrying the dynamic
7	 * background-image fill — the URL itself cannot live here, see the component's own comment on

13	 */

15	  parts: ['swatch', 'image'],
16	
17	  baseStyle: ({ selected }: { selected?: boolean }): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
18	    swatch: {
19	      display: 'inline-block',
20	      cursor: 'pointer',
21	      // Figma's Rectangle width (48px). Height (72px) has no direct token — the named scale has
22	      // nothing between 64px and 140px — so it's expressed as an aspect ratio on the width
23	      // instead. 2:3, not the incidentally different ratio Figma's raw code-gen attached to the
24	      // placeholder product photo pasted into that frame instance: the Selected-state node
25	      // carries its own dev annotation reading "Image aspect ratio - 2:3", which is the number
26	      // to trust here.
27	      width: 'var(--zimm-scale-1200)',
28	      aspectRatio: '2 / 3',
29	      // Identical across Unselected/Selected/Focus — ivory[200] / background['02'] in
30	      // theme/foundation/colour.ts.
31	      backgroundColor: 'var(--zimm-color-bg-02)',
32	      // Selected: a bottom-only border — the raw Figma export is unambiguous, a `border-b`
33	      // utility rather than a full box border. Colour is grey[900] / border.focus, the only
34	      // alias-tier value that resolves to it (border.default and border.secondary are both
35	      // light greys and never appear anywhere in this design).
36	      ...(selected
37	        ? {
38	            borderBottomWidth: 'var(--zimm-border-width-default)',
39	            borderBottomStyle: 'solid',
40	            borderBottomColor: 'var(--zimm-color-border-focus)',
41	          }
42	        : {}),
43	      // Focus: Figma draws this as the Selected baseline plus a ring at slightly asymmetric
44	      // per-side offsets, same colour. Not replicated literally — there is no other precedent

46	      // frame instance's export noise rather than a deliberate design decision. Mirrors

50	      // same border-width/colour pair used above; `--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default` matches
51	      // three of Figma's four side offsets.

53	        outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)',
54	        outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)',
55	      },

/**
 * Recipe for the PDP meta block — the model line and the style code, which the design places
 * at the bottom of the info column below the accordions.
 *
 * Multipart with a single `root` part rather than a bare `baseStyle`: `ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts`
 * reconciles a declared `parts` array against what the sibling component actually reads off
 * `useMultiStyleConfig`, and a recipe with no `parts` key is skipped by that walk entirely.
 * Declaring the one part buys the reconciliation for the two-node shape this block will grow
 * into when the designer settles the label/value question raised in `zimmProductStyleCode.css.ts`.
 */

/**
 * DS: 28px between the drawers and the model line, and again between the model line and the
 * style code — identical on both breakpoints (pdp/product-content, desktop and mobile Default).
 * Figma: pdp/product-content, Desktop Default 40000307:14062 / Mobile Default 40000343:9727.
 *
 * A rem literal because no rem-valued 28px token exists to reference. `spacing.ts` brackets it
 * at `xl` (1.5rem/24px) and `2xl` (2rem/32px) with nothing between, and `--zimm-scale-700` — the
 * one alias that does hold 28px — is itself a raw px string in `zimmTokens.ts`, not a reference
 * to a named step the way its neighbours `--zimm-scale-600`/`-800` reference `spacing.xl`/`2xl`.
 * Substituting it would silently convert spacing that scales with the user's root font size into
 * fixed px, which is what overrideStyling.md's Units rule rules out for spacing (WCAG 1.4.4).
 *
 * `theme/components/listMenu.ts` (lines 17, 33, 65, 84) does use `var(--zimm-scale-700)` for its
 * own 28px, so the precedent in this repo is genuinely split — noted here so the next reader does
 * not read that file as evidence this one is wrong and "align" it into a px value. The Units rule
 * is what decides, and it points at rem for spacing. Pending a named 28px step from the UI
 * designer both should converge on; listMenu.ts is designer-owned Tier 2 and not this file's to
 * change. Do not swap for `xl` or `2xl`, both visibly wrong.
 */
const SPACE_META_ROW = '1.75rem'; // 28px at the default 16px root

export const ZimmProductMeta = {
  parts: ['root'],
  baseStyle: {
    // One const drives both hops because the design measures both at 28px. Written as a `gap`
    // plus a `paddingTop` on the same container — the pattern `footer.css.ts` (lines 41-42)
    // already uses with its own SPACE_SECTION — so the two cannot drift apart.
    root: {
      display: 'flex',
      flexDirection: 'column',
      alignItems: 'flex-start',
      gap: SPACE_META_ROW, // model line -> style code
      paddingTop: SPACE_META_ROW, // drawers -> model line
    },
  },
};

} & ({ 'aria-hidden': true; 'aria-label'?: never } | { 'aria-hidden'?: never; 'aria-label': string });

const ICON_MAP = {
  'arrow-down': ArrowDownIcon,
  'arrow-link': ArrowLinkIcon,
  'arrow-up': ArrowUpIcon,
  bag: BagIcon,
  'bag-selected': BagSelectedIcon,
  calendar: CalendarIcon,
  carousel: CarouselIcon,
  'carousel-selected': CarouselSelectedIcon,
  chat: ChatIcon,
  check: CheckIcon,
  'chevron-down': ChevronDownIcon,
  'chevron-left': ChevronLeftIcon,
  'chevron-right': ChevronRightIcon,
  'chevron-up': ChevronUpIcon,
  close: CloseIcon,
  delete: DeleteIcon,
  edit: EditIcon,
  'external-link': ExternalLinkIcon,
  info: InfoIcon,
  'info-selected': InfoSelectedIcon,
  location: LocationIcon,
  menu: MenuIcon,
  minus: MinusIcon,
  mute: MuteIcon,
  password: PasswordShowIcon,
  pause: PauseIcon,
  play: PlayIcon,
  plus: PlusIcon,
  profile: ProfileIcon,
  search: SearchIcon,
  share: ShareIcon,
  'share-2': ShareTwoIcon,
  wishlist: FavouritesIcon,
  'wishlist-selected': FavouritesSolidIcon,
  // Footer-specific custom icons — not yet in Figma node 1892:59595,
  // pending addition to the iconography spec in the next design sync.
  phone: PhoneIcon,
  whatsapp: WhatsAppIcon,
  email: EmailIcon,
} as const;

/** Atom — single icon from the Zimmermann icon set. Mirrors zimm-icon contract. */
export const ZimmIcon = ({ type, size = 'md', color = 'currentColor', ...aria }: ZimmIconProps) => {
  const Icon = ICON_MAP[type];
  // Both keys exist in every member of the union (one required, one optional-`never`), so the
  // rest object is indexable directly. The XOR is enforced by ZimmIconProps, not by a cast —
  // casting here only widened 'aria-hidden' from `true | undefined` to `boolean | undefined`.
  const ariaHidden = aria['aria-hidden'];
  const ariaLabel = aria['aria-label'];
  return (
    <Icon
      boxSize={iconSizes[size]}
      color={color}
      aria-hidden={ariaHidden}
      aria-label={ariaLabel}
      role={ariaLabel ? 'img' : undefined}
    />
  );
};

1	import React from 'react';
2	import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
3	import { ZimmIcon } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon';
4	import { isSafeHref } from 'app/utils/safeHref';
5	
6	const ZIMM_CONTACT_ICON_ROW_RECIPE = 'ZimmContactIconRow';
7	
8	// Figma: Icon-list has pt-4px (alias/space/100) above it and 4px internal gap between icons.
9	// hrefs are typically sourced from Contentful (FooterConfigEntry, HPC-034) by the caller. Until
10	// that integration lands, absent hrefs render each icon as a non-interactive but labelled
11	// <span> — visible in the layout and announced by screen readers, but absent from the tab
12	// order. See the inline note on the fallback branch below for the full a11y reasoning. When a
13	// href arrives it switches to a live <a>, no other changes needed.
14	type ZimmContactIconRowProps = {
15	  phoneHref?: string; // locale-aware tel: href
16	  whatsAppHref?: string; // WhatsApp URL
17	  emailHref?: string; // mailto: address
18	};
19	
20	type ContactLink = { href?: string; label: string; icon: 'phone' | 'whatsapp' | 'email' };
21	
22	/**
23	 * True when following the href would navigate away from the storefront.
24	 *
25	 * Takes `string | undefined` rather than `string` so the caller does not need an `as string` to
26	 * satisfy it inside an isSafeHref branch. isSafeHref returns a plain boolean, which carries no
27	 * narrowing, and a `href is string` predicate would be unsound — an unsafe value like
28	 * `javascript:void(0)` is a string that returns false, so the else branch would narrow to
29	 * `undefined` incorrectly. An absent href never leaves the site, so `?? ''` is the honest answer.
30	 *
31	 * Derived from the scheme rather than keyed to a channel name: tel: and mailto: hand off to the
32	 * OS dialer or mail client and never navigate, so a target on them does nothing. An http(s)
33	 * channel — WhatsApp today — is a real cross-origin navigation and opens in a new tab so a
34	 * shopper mid-browse does not lose the site. Any future http(s) channel inherits this without
35	 * another edit here.
36	 */
37	const leavesTheSite = (href: string | undefined): boolean => /^https?:/i.test(href ?? '');
38	
39	/** WCAG 3.2.5 — a link that opens a new tab has to say so in its accessible name. */
40	const NEW_TAB_SUFFIX = ' — opens in a new tab';
41	
42	/**
43	 * Contact channel icon row (phone / WhatsApp / email). Extracted from the footer so it can be
44	 * reused anywhere a storefront needs the same channels — nothing here is footer-specific.
45	 *
46	 * @param props see ZimmContactIconRowProps
47	 */
48	export const ZimmContactIconRow = ({ phoneHref, whatsAppHref, emailHref }: ZimmContactIconRowProps) => {
49	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_CONTACT_ICON_ROW_RECIPE, {});
50	  const links: ContactLink[] = [
51	    { href: phoneHref, label: 'Call us', icon: 'phone' },
52	    { href: whatsAppHref, label: 'WhatsApp', icon: 'whatsapp' },
53	    { href: emailHref, label: 'Email us', icon: 'email' },
54	  ];
55	  return (
56	    <chakra.div __css={styles.row}>
57	      {links.map(({ href, label, icon }) =>
58	        // isSafeHref, not a truthiness check: these typically arrive from Contentful, so a
59	        // javascript:/data:/protocol-relative value would otherwise be rendered straight onto
60	        // an anchor. Rejected values fall through to the span below, which is already the
61	        // correct treatment for "no usable destination".
62	        isSafeHref(href) ? (
63	          <chakra.a
64	            key={icon}
65	            href={href}
66	            // rel is explicit rather than relying on target="_blank" implying noopener: that is
67	            // browser default behaviour, not a guarantee, and noreferrer also stops the
68	            // storefront URL leaking to the third party.
69	            {...(leavesTheSite(href) ? { target: '_blank', rel: 'noopener noreferrer' } : {})}
70	            aria-label={leavesTheSite(href) ? `${label}${NEW_TAB_SUFFIX}` : label}
71	            __css={styles.iconLink}
72	          >
73	            <ZimmIcon type={icon} size="md" aria-hidden={true} />
74	          </chakra.a>
75	        ) : (
76	          // Fallback for a channel with no usable destination — either the field is absent, or
77	          // isSafeHref rejected the value. Both reach here, and both want the same treatment.
78	          // NON-INTERACTIVE but PERCEIVABLE:
79	          //   - <span>: no href, no tabIndex, so nothing promises an action that cannot be
80	          //     performed (avoids the WCAG 2.4.4 / 3.2.4 false affordance).
81	          //   - labelled, not aria-hidden: ZimmIcon emits role="img" + aria-label, so screen
82	          //     reader users learn the channel exists instead of getting silence (avoids the
83	          //     1.1.1 information loss the previous aria-hidden caused).
84	          // Not dead code: contact channels are optional per storefront, so a locale that
85	          // supplies only e.g. email still renders the other two icons this way.
86	          <chakra.span key={icon} __css={styles.iconLink}>
87	            <ZimmIcon type={icon} size="md" aria-label={label} />
88	          </chakra.span>
89	        ),
90	      )}
91	    </chakra.div>
92	  );
93	};

8	import React, {Children, useCallback, useEffect, useRef, useState} from 'react'
9	import PropTypes from 'prop-types'
10	import {
11	    Flex,
12	    Box,
13	    HStack,
14	    useStyleConfig
15	} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui'
16	import {FormattedMessage} from 'react-intl'
17	import {noop} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/utils'
18	
19	const DIRECTIONS = {
20	    FORWARD: 1,
21	    BACKWARD: -1
22	}
23	
24	/**
25	 * SwatchGroup allows you to create a list of swatches
26	 * Each Swatch is a link with will direct to a href passed to them
27	 */
28	const SwatchGroup = (props) => {
29	    const {ariaLabel, displayName, children, label = '', value, handleChange = noop} = props
30	
31	    const styles = useStyleConfig('SwatchGroup')
32	    const [selectedIndex, setSelectedIndex] = useState(0)
33	    const wrapperRef = useRef(null)
34	
35	    // Handle keyboard navigation.
36	    const onKeyDown = useCallback(
37	        (e) => {
38	            const {key} = e
39	            const move = (direction = DIRECTIONS.FORWARD) => {
40	                let index = selectedIndex + direction // forward = +1 backwards = -1
41	                index = (selectedIndex + direction) % children.length // keep number in bounds of array with modulus
42	                index = index < 0 ? children.length - Math.abs(index) : Math.abs(index) // We we are dealing with a negative we have to invert the index
43	
44	                // Get a reference to the newly selected swatch as we are going to focus it later.
45	                const swatchEl = wrapperRef?.current?.children[index]
46	
47	                // Set the new index that is always in the arrays range.
48	                setSelectedIndex(index)
49	
50	                // Behave like a radio button a focus the new swatch.
51	                swatchEl?.focus()
52	            }
53	
54	            switch (key) {
55	                case 'ArrowUp':
56	                case 'ArrowLeft':
57	                    e.preventDefault()
58	                    move(DIRECTIONS.BACKWARD)
59	                    break
60	                case 'ArrowDown':
61	                case 'ArrowRight':
62	                    e.preventDefault()
63	                    move(DIRECTIONS.FORWARD)
64	                    break
65	                default:
66	                    break
67	            }
68	        },
69	        [selectedIndex]
70	    )
71	
72	    // Initialize the component state on mount, this includes the selected index value.
73	    useEffect(() => {
74	        if (!value) {
75	            return
76	        }
77	        const childrenArray = Children.toArray(children)
78	        const index = childrenArray.findIndex(({props}) => props?.value === value)
79	
80	        setSelectedIndex(index)
81	    }, [])
82	
83	    // Whenever the selected index changes ensure that we call the change handler.
84	    useEffect(() => {
85	        const childrenArray = Children.toArray(children)
86	        if (childrenArray[selectedIndex]) {
87	            const newValue = childrenArray[selectedIndex].props.value
88	            handleChange(newValue)
89	        }
90	    }, [selectedIndex])
91	
92	    return (
93	        <Box onKeyDown={onKeyDown}>
94	            <Flex {...styles.swatchGroup} role="radiogroup" aria-label={ariaLabel || label}>
95	                {label && (
96	                    <HStack {...styles.swatchLabel}>
97	                        <Box fontWeight="semibold">
98	                            <FormattedMessage
99	                                id="swatch_group.selected.label"
100	                                defaultMessage="{label}:"
101	                                values={{label}}
102	                            />
103	                        </Box>
104	                        <Box>{displayName}</Box>
105	                    </HStack>
106	                )}
107	                <Flex ref={wrapperRef} {...styles.swatchesWrapper}>
108	                    {Children.toArray(children).map((child, index) => {
109	                        const selected = child.props.value === value
110	                        return React.cloneElement(child, {
111	                            handleSelect: handleChange,
112	                            selected,
113	                            isFocusable: value ? selected : index === 0
114	                        })
115	                    })}
116	                </Flex>
117	            </Flex>
118	        </Box>
119	    )
120	}
121	
122	SwatchGroup.displayName = 'SwatchGroup'
123	
124	SwatchGroup.propTypes = {
125	    /**
126	     * The aria label to be used on the group. If none is provided we will
127	     * use the label prop.
128	     */
129	    ariaLabel: PropTypes.string,
130	    /**
131	     * The attribute name of the swatch group. E.g color, size
132	     */
133	    label: PropTypes.string,
134	    /**
135	     * The display value of the selected option
136	     */
137	    displayName: PropTypes.string,
138	    /**
139	     * The Swatch options to choose between
140	     */
141	    children: PropTypes.node,
142	    /**
143	     * This function is called whenever the selected swatch changes.
144	     */
145	    handleChange: PropTypes.func,
146	    /**
147	     * The currentvalue for the option.
148	     */
149	    value: PropTypes.string
150	}
151	
152	export default SwatchGroup

2	
3	// Shared between footer's split recipe files (footer.css.ts, footerNavColumn.css.ts,
4	// bottomBar.css.ts) so a breakpoint or provisional size can't drift between them the way a
5	// copy-pasted literal would. Not a general-purpose theme module — scope stays footer-only; see
6	// .claude/rules/overrideStyling.md's co-location guidance for why these no longer live in one
7	// flat theme/components/footer.ts.
8	
9	// `tablet` mirrors the confirmed foundation token `breakpoints.md` — imported rather than
10	// retyped so the two cannot drift apart. `tabletWide` and `desktop` have no foundation
11	// equivalent yet; `desktop` additionally conflicts with Chakra's lg (62em) and xl (80em), which
12	// is why every desktop rule using this constant is a raw @media rather than a responsive prop.
13	// Media queries cannot consume var(), so this is the one deliberate exception to
14	// theme/components/ otherwise avoiding direct foundation/ imports in favour of --zimm-* CSS vars.
15	// audit-allow: raw em is correct and permanent here, not a placeholder awaiting a token —
16	// overrideStyling.md's Units section documents breakpoints as one of the few genuinely
17	// context-relative uses of em, deliberately outside the var(--zimm-*) scale system.
18	export const BP = {
19	  tablet: breakpoints.md, // Figma: alias/breakpoint/tablet — 768px
20	  tabletWide: '53.75em', // Figma: alias/breakpoint/tablet-wide — 860px (no foundation equivalent)
21	  desktop: '64em', // Figma: alias/breakpoint/desktop — 1024px (≠ Chakra lg=62em / xl=80em)
22	} as const;
23	
24	// alias/size/footer/col-width-nav (140px). Provisional — kept as a named rem reference until
25	// the UI designer confirms it in foundation/sizes.ts. Used by both the nav column's own width
26	// (footerNavColumn.css.ts) and the bottom bar's mobile legal-link width (bottomBar.css.ts) — the
27	// two must match or the legal links stop lining up with the columns above them.
28	export const SIZE_COL_NAV = '8.75rem';

1	import React from 'react';
2	import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
3	import { useIntl } from 'react-intl';
4	
5	const ZIMM_PRODUCT_STYLE_CODE_RECIPE = 'ZimmProductStyleCode';
6	
7	/*
8	 * The label is UI copy, so it is a translatable message rather than a literal. `defaultMessage`
9	 * carries the English inline, which is what makes this work with no `translations/` entry: that
10	 * directory is Tier 2 (owner Integration/SI Partner) and is populated by the extraction step, so
11	 * a component cannot add to it. Until extraction runs, every locale renders `defaultMessage`;
12	 * once it does, the eleven locales pick up their own string with no change here.
13	 *
14	 * The id follows the base template's namespace for PDP labels — `product_view.label.quantity`
15	 * and `product_view.label.variant_type` are its siblings — so a translator finds it with the
16	 * rest of the PDP copy.
17	 */
18	const LABEL_MESSAGE = {
19	  id: 'product_view.label.style_code',
20	  defaultMessage: 'Style Code:',
21	};
22	
23	type ZimmProductStyleCodeProps = {
24	  /**
25	   * The master product's style number. This is the style code shown to shoppers, which is not
26	   * the same value as the variant `product.id`.
27	   */
28	  value?: string;
29	};
30	
31	/**
32	 * Atom — the "Style Code: 7300JS261" line. Renders nothing when no style code is available.
33	 *
34	 * The label comes from `react-intl`, not from CMS microcopy and not from a literal. A `uiCopy`
35	 * lookup is the wrong tool here — `useContentful.ts` requests entries with no `locale`
36	 * parameter, so it would serve the space default to all eight storefronts regardless of site —
37	 * but a bare literal is not the remedy for that, it just ships English to all eleven locales
38	 * instead. `formatMessage` is the base template's own mechanism and is per-locale by
39	 * construction.
40	 *
41	 * components.md exempts `useIntl` from the container/presentational rule: it reads a Provider
42	 * mounted above the route tree, so calling it from a leaf creates none of the per-page fetch
43	 * problems that rule exists to prevent. It does *throw* without an `IntlProvider` — the app
44	 * mounts one in the base `_app`, `.storybook/preview.tsx` mounts one for stories, and
45	 * `index.test.tsx` wraps its renders for the same reason.
46	 */
47	export const ZimmProductStyleCode = ({ value }: ZimmProductStyleCodeProps) => {
48	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_PRODUCT_STYLE_CODE_RECIPE, {});
49	  // `intl.formatMessage`, not a destructured `{ formatMessage }`: destructuring a method off
50	  // `useIntl()` trips `@typescript-eslint/unbound-method`, which `staticProductHeader.tsx` has to
51	  // suppress inline. `product-view/index.tsx` uses this form throughout and needs no suppression.
52	  const intl = useIntl();
53	  // Both hooks sit above the guard: an early return before either makes that call conditional,
54	  // which `react-hooks/rules-of-hooks` reports as an error. Same ordering as the sibling atoms.
55	  if (!value) return null;
56	
57	  return (
58	    <chakra.div __css={styles.root} data-testid="product-style-code">
59	      <chakra.span __css={styles.label}>{intl.formatMessage(LABEL_MESSAGE)}</chakra.span>
60	      {/*
61	        A real space so `textContent` — what a screen reader reads out and what a shopper
62	        copies — is "Style Code: 8637DS241", matching both composed page designs. It adds no
63	        visual width: a whitespace-only anonymous flex item is not rendered (CSS Flexbox §4),
64	        so the 4px `gap` in the recipe remains the only spacing.
65	      */}{' '}
66	      <chakra.span __css={styles.value}>{value}</chakra.span>
67	    </chakra.div>
68	  );
69	};
